scope: Publication title, metadata, source reproducibility, finite exact and symbolic controls, and PDF/artifact verification. Not independent mathematical certification, and not a page-by-page visual review of the pages this edition changed.
title: Five-Step Descent Certificates for the Juggler Map: Parity Statistics of Nested Floor Powers
digest_convention: Text digests are taken over content, with CRLF and CR normalised to LF, as tools/artifact_digest.py does. pdf_sha256 and source_zip_sha256 are raw bytes, which is what a downloaded file holds. The 2026-09-10 record hashed text raw, so its source_sha256 described the packager's checkout rather than the manuscript, and it named an edition eleven revisions old.
mathematical_body_definition: SHA-256 of the manuscript after its closing YAML fence, leading newlines removed, line endings normalised to LF; the digested text begins '## Abstract'. The 2026-09-10 record printed a body digest that no line-aligned slice of its own deposited files reproduces.

sections_changed: 6. The fixed-depth reduction to density-one certificates
changes_since_the_proof_audit_edition.summary: The threshold in Theorem 6.1 is now the largest the step admits rather than a convenient one, its Chernoff and density steps carry Lean cross-references, and Remark 6.2 identifies the resulting exponent with the Cramer rate of the underlying walk. Theorem 6.1 remains conditional on the fair-share hypothesis, which is not formalised.
changes_since_the_proof_audit_edition.unchanged: The abstract, Sections 1-5, Sections 7-8, Appendices A-C, the acknowledgments and the references are byte-identical to the 2026-09-10 proof-audit edition, so Theorem 5.4 and its error exponent are untouched.

review_report: paper_b_proof_review.md; the 10 September audit applies unchanged to every section except Section 6, which postdates it and has had no independent audit.
symbolic_derivation: PASS; rerun with SymPy 1.14.0 on the extracted source, reproducing -243/512, 3645/2048, and 81/512.
standalone_source_rebuild: PASS; the source archive was extracted into an empty directory and rebuilt with its own build_paper_b.py. The generated LaTeX is byte-identical to the delivered LaTeX, and so is the PDF, because SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is pinned to the edition. The consolidated controls and the symbolic review rerun there agree with the repository.
standalone_rebuild_repair: The 2026-09-16 change that moved the build work directory to the repository root broke `python build_paper_b.py` inside an extracted package, which is the command PAPER_B_BUILD.md gives a reviewer: there is no repository root there, so the path was built from None. The work directory now falls back to the output tree.
archive_determinism: PASS; the archives are a function of the commit. Text members are written LF, member stamps come from the pinned build epoch, and no packager operating system is recorded, so two people packaging one commit produce the same bytes.
archive_integrity_and_checksums: PASS; both archives pass zipfile.testzip, and `python tools/build_paper_b_kit.py --check` verifies every member against the repository, both in-archive SHA256SUMS.txt files against their own members, and the kit SHA256SUMS.txt against the files beside it.
checksum_staleness_repaired: The 2026-09-10 kit failed `sha256sum -c` on its own PDF: build_paper_b.py --sync refreshes the PDF alias in the kit while nothing refreshed SHA256SUMS.txt or this record beside it. The kit is now generated by tools/build_paper_b_kit.py, and the paper release gate runs its --check.

visual_review.method: Every page of both editions rendered at 100 dpi with Poppler and compared pixel by pixel.
visual_review.changed: page 1, which carries the edition date, and pages 14-37
visual_review.human_page_by_page_review: OUTSTANDING for the 27 changed and new pages. The 10 September audit's page-by-page review covers only the 12 pages that are still pixel-identical. Pages 14 and 39 were spot-checked and render clean, with no clipping, overlap or broken tables.
